Apinan Soottitantawat
Department of Chemical Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Chulalongkorn University

Three parts

What we will answer

1What must the equipment list and datasheets say, and where does each number come from?→ 2How thick must the adsorber be, and how many pressure cycles must it survive?→ 3What else does the cycle demand of the valves, the internals and the cooler?→

EQL = equipment list · ASME VIII = the pressure-vessel code (Division 1 sizing, Division 2 fatigue) · PSV = pressure safety valve · FV = full vacuum · CA = corrosion allowance · XV = switching valve. Document VPSA-V1-ME-EQL-001; tags follow the P&ID tab.

What must the equipment list and datasheets say, and where does each number come from?

VPSA-V1-ME-EQL-001 · part 1

The equipment list is the mechanical master

One line per item

Service, type, size, design pressure and temperature, material.

Sizes from the model

V-100 holds 20 m³ because the simulator's K.V100 does.

Choices marked assumed

Design pressures, T/T lengths and materials are engineering choices.

Procurement, layout, relief and the electrical load list all read it.

Interactive · pick an item of the EQL

Every line, with the model value beside it

The sizes match the model; the design conditions are choices made with the model's range in view.

Rule of thumb used in this document

Design pressure sits above the relief set, which sits above operation

The model gives the operating range; the EQL must stay clear of it.

$P_{op,max}$
highest pressure in four normal model runs
bar a
$P_{set}$
PSV set pressure (P&ID relief list)
bar a
$P_{d}$
design pressure on the EQL
bar a
$P_d\ \ge\ P_{set}\ \ge\ 1.10\,P_{op,max}$

A 10 % margin keeps the PSV from simmering at the top of the cycle.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • The EQL carries one line per item; sizes come from the model.
  • Design, PSV set and 1.10 × operating hold in every normal run.
  • PIC-133 at 1.5 bar a brings V-103 within 5 % of its PSV.
  • A datasheet names the source of every value.

Worked numbers · V-101A/B, 7 bar a design, ID 1910 mm

Internal pressure needs only 5.7 mm

Previous slide$t_{shell}=PR/(SE-0.6P),\quad t_{head}=PD/(2SE-0.2P)$
$P=7.0-1.013=5.987\ \text{bar g}=0.5987\ \text{MPa}$EQL design pressure, to gauge
$t_{shell}=\dfrac{0.5987\times956.5}{138\times1.0-0.6\times0.5987}=4.16\ \text{mm}$R = 955 + 1.5 mm CA
$4.16+1.5=5.66\ \text{mm};\quad t_{head}=4.15+1.5=5.65\ \text{mm}$add the corrosion allowance

Yet the EQL shell is 14 mm: another load governs.

External pressure · step 1 of 2

Under vacuum a thin shell buckles before it yields

The beds are evacuated to 0.1 bar a every cycle, so the shell is squeezed from outside.

$D_o,\ L$
outside diameter; T/T + 2/3 of each head depth
mm
$P_{cr},\ P_a$
elastic buckling pressure; allowable external
MPa
$E_s,\ \nu,\ S_y$
steel: 200 000, 0.3, yield 260
MPa, –, MPa
$P_{cr}=\dfrac{2.42\,E_s\,(t/D_o)^{2.5}}{(1-\nu^2)^{0.75}\big(L/D_o-0.45\sqrt{t/D_o}\big)},\quad P_a=\min\!\Big(\dfrac{P_{cr}}{3},\ \dfrac{2S_y t}{3D_o}\Big)$

Windenburg–Trilling, the elastic basis of the UG-28 chart; a screening only.

External pressure · step 2 of 2 · design 0.103 MPa (15 psi, assumed)

Full vacuum sets a 14 mm shell

Previous slide$P_a=\min\big(P_{cr}/3,\ 2S_yt/3D_o\big)\ \ge\ 0.103\ \text{MPa}$
$L=7000+2\times\tfrac{1910/4}{3}=7318\ \text{mm}$2:1 head depth is D/4
$t=10.75:\ D_o=1934.5,\ P_{cr}=0.319,\ P_a=0.106\ \text{MPa}$thinnest corroded shell that passes
$10.75+1.5=12.25\ \rightarrow\ 14\ \text{mm plate}$next standard plate

2.2 × the pressure case; stiffening rings would cut it.

Fatigue screening · step 1 of 2 · VIII-2 5.5.2.3, Method A

Count the cycles before computing any stress

$t_{c}$
full cycle (one KS-140 sequence): two half cycles of 448.875 s (model)
s
$n,\ h$
pressure cycles per bed a year; continuous 8760 h year (EPC counting basis, conservative)
1/yr, h
$\Delta P/P_d$
cycle range over design pressure (gauge)
–
$n=\dfrac{h\cdot3600}{t_c},\qquad \dfrac{\Delta P}{P_d}>20\ \%\ \Rightarrow\ \text{significant},\qquad \text{days}=\dfrac{1000}{n}\times365$

Method A skips the fatigue analysis only up to 1000 significant cycles.

Fatigue screening · step 2 of 2 · design cycle of the model

The screening allowance is gone in 10 days

Previous slide$n=h\cdot3600/t_c,\quad \text{days}=1000/n\times365$
$t_c=2\times448.875=897.75\ \text{s};\quad n=\dfrac{8760\times3600}{897.75}=35\,128\ \text{yr}^{-1}$0.703 million in 20 years
$\Delta P=4.572-0.097=4.48\ \text{bar}=75\ \%\ \text{of}\ 5.99\ \text{bar g}$above 20 %: every cycle counts
$1000\,/\,35\,128\times365=10.4\ \text{days}$then a fatigue analysis is due

Method A fails: a fatigue analysis is required (EQ-emech-1).

EQ-emech-1 · cyclic service not stated on the EQL

Write the cycle onto the datasheet

Cycles, pressure range, temperature: VIII-2 Part 5 applies.

Detail the welds

Full-penetration nozzles, ground smooth.

Fix the thin vessel

V-100: thicker plate or better nozzle detail.

Inspect in service

Nozzle welds of beds and receiver.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Internal pressure needs 5.7 mm; full vacuum sets the 14 mm shell.
  • Each bed sees 35 128 pressure cycles a year.
  • The 1000-cycle screening allowance lasts 10 days.
  • Nozzle welds govern: U 0.55 for the beds, 3.91 for V-100 at 8 mm.

Interactive · step the KS-140 sequence (STEPS × MODES)

Four valves per bed make the eight steps

XV-114 opens twice per cycle (equalisation and purge); the others once.

Interactive · openings from the sequencer and the model's half cycle (1 opening = 2 strokes)

A million openings, each against a pressure difference

At 20 years on 8760 h XV-114 opens 1.41 × 10⁶ times (2.81 × 10⁶ strokes), inside a 2 × 10⁶-cycle rating (assumed).

Selection table of the document · part 6

What a switching valve must be

XV-111A: actuator, solenoid, limit switches · AI-generated illustration (Gemini)

  • Tight shut-off for a million cycles.
  • Fail closed on air or power loss.
  • Oxygen-service trim on XV-113/114 (O2S class).
  • Limited opening speed where ΔP is 4.5 bar.
  • Limit switches prove each stroke.

Engineering queries raised by this document

Where two documents disagree, the query is the lesson

EQ-emech-2 · E-100

86 kW assumed 138 °C from a two-stage machine; the package aftercooler delivers 45 °C.

EQ-emech-3 · K-101 · resolved

Rev B note: about 6900 m³/h. The model pump, 3240 m³/h, was kept; P&ID rev C now agrees.

EQ-emech-5 · PSV-103

Raise the set below the 4.5 bar a design, or limit PIC-133.

The Project & deliverables tab collects every query.

Interactive · 45 checks recomputed from the model and the EQL

Checks against the model and the other documents

40 ✓ and 5 ✗; every ✗ is an engineering query, not a hidden error.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • XV-114 opens twice a cycle: 1.41 × 10⁶ openings in 20 years.
  • Upflow of 529 mbar lifts a 462 mbar bed: hold-down needed.
  • The model's NTU relation rates E-100 at 25.6 kW.
  • Five ✗ checks stay open as queries; the K-101 one closed with P&ID rev C.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Put the model value beside every equipment-list line.

2

Keep design ≥ PSV set ≥ 1.10 × the highest operating pressure.

3

Check vacuum: buckling, not stress, sets the adsorber shell.

4

Treat every adsorber and receiver as cyclic service.

5

Raise a query where two documents disagree; do not hide it.
